notes: The opposite is 富 (fù, 'rich') or 有钱 (yǒuqián, 'wealthy').

senses.definition: Having little money or few possessions.

examples.text: 他小时候家里很穷，连书都买不起。
examples.translation: When he was a child, his family was very poor and couldn't even afford books.
examples.emotion: melancholy and reflective, recalling a difficult past

draftBefore.emotion: heavy and weary, carrying the weight of financial struggle
notes: Commonly used to describe having little or no money.
Do not confuse with 累 (lèi), which means tired.

senses.definition: Having little money or few possessions; lacking sufficient money to live at a standard considered comfortable or normal.

examples.text: 他小时候家里很穷，连书都买不起。
examples.translation: When he was a child, his family was very poor and couldn't even afford books.
examples.emotion: melancholy and reflective, recalling a difficult past

senses.definition: Reaching an extreme limit or coming to an end, often used in set phrases to describe running out of options.

examples.text: 事情到了这一步，已经是穷途末路了。
examples.translation: Things have reached this point; it is truly the end of the road.
examples.emotion: desperate and hopeless, seeing no way forward

faults.quote: Reaching an extreme limit or coming to an end
faults.why: Literary bound morpheme found only in idioms, not an A2 adjective sense.

faults.quote: Commonly used to describe having little or no money.
Do not confuse with 累 (lèi), which means tired.
faults.why: Unmotivated comparison; learners have no reason to confuse 穷 and 累.
